Sofia Rei’s performances with Jorge Roeder have blown us away. Tonite she introduces a new project and we are looking forward!

Sofia Rei ~ Vocals
JC Maillard ~ Guitar

Award-winning vocalist, composer, and producer Sofía Rei joins forces with longtime collaborator and guitarist JC Maillard for an intimate acoustic duo performance.
Born in Buenos Aires and based in New York, Rei has developed a distinctive musical language that bridges South American folk traditions, jazz, and experimental music. Praised by The New York Times and DownBeat for her versatility, she moves effortlessly between delicate expression, adventurous improvisation, and electrifying intensity.
Together, Rei and Maillard strip the music down to its essentials, exploring the interplay of voice and guitar through original compositions, improvisation, and fresh interpretations of Latin American traditions.

E.J. Strickland has toured, performed, and recorded with some of the greatest names in contemporary music: Cassandra Wilson, Terence Blanchard, Lizz Wright, Wynton Marsalis, George Colligan, David Gilmore, Vincent Herring, and Nnenna Freelon. As an instructor, he's taught alongside Dave Douglas and Vijay Iyer at the prestigious Banff International Workshop in Jazz & Creative Music, Steve Kirby at University of Manitoba, and Earl MacDonald at University of Connecticut.

As a leader, he's released two albums: In This Day featuring Marcus Strickland, Jaleel Shaw, Luis Perdomo, and Hans Glawischnig. His most recent release, The Undying Spirit "positively glows…its success comes largely from the leader's ability to inspire the best in his fellow musicians," says Brian Zimmerman, Downbeat Magazine.

Founded in the spirit of the present moment, Transient Beings celebrates the one thing we all share: limited time on Earth.

The bandstand always lights up with Vinícius Gomes in the mix.. Tonite he leads this killler Brazilian ensemble — who will pay homage to the masters of Música Popular Brasileira, a term as broad as the musical styles it embraces. You don’t want to miss this electric lineup!

Vinícius Gomes ~ guitar
Jamile ~ vocals
Fernando Saci ~ percussion
Henrique Eisenman ~ piano
Gili Lopes ~ bass
Dennis Bulhōes ~ drums


VINÍCIUS GOMES is a Brazilian jazz guitarist, composer, and first-call sideman. His sound weds Brazilian classical, jazz, and American jazz traditions to the advanced chromatics of Baden Powell, Pat Metheny, and Julian Lage. His acclaimed 2017 debut Resiliência appeared on Blaxtream, with backing from a cast which included drummer Edu Ribeiro, saxophonist Rodrigo Ursaia, bassist Bruno Migotto, and pianist Gustavo Bugni. In 2020, he and saxophonist Santi De La Rubia collaborated on the album Changes; its extended lineup included drummer Jorge Rossy and bassist Doug Weiss. Gomes is known internationally as one of Brazil's finest accompanists for vocalists; he was worked extensively with Zizi Possi, Rosa Passos, and Jane Duboc as both an accompanist and music director.

***$10 (CASH) SUGGESTED DONATION***

Wayne Tucker & The Bad Mothas remain one of NYC’s tightest ensembles. Tonite they sport a double keyboard rhythm section. Come check it out!

Wayne Tucker - Trumpet and Vocals
Miles Tucker - Tenor Sax
Addison Frei - Keys
David Linard - Piano
Julian Miltenberger - Drums

WAYNE TUCKER is a trumpeter, composer, arranger, violinist, vocalist, actor and model based in New York City. He has released 5 albums under his name and performs regularly with his band, The Bad Mothas in New York City.

Wayne has toured and recorded with a diverse array of notables such as jazz musicians Kurt Elling, Dee Dee Bridgewater and Cyrille Aimée; pop acts Taylor Swift, David Crosby, Elvis Costello; r&b singers Ne-Yo and Gabriel Garzon-Montano; hip hop artists Jidenna and Ryan Leslie; and with the rock band Brass Against.

This diversity is represented in The Bad Mothas energetic sound where the American Songbook gets a welcome update, including selections by Michael Jackson or Earth Wind & Fire.  Tenor saxophonist Miles Tucker (Wayne's brother) holds a lean mean counterpoint to Wayne's gentle affability on trumpet. Drummer Diego Joaquin Ramirez and bassist Tamir Shmerling provide solid underpinning which accommodates a varied cast of pianists, most notably the gospel-influenced Willerm Delisfort.  The group was featured in the New York Times for its steady schedule of street performances during the 2020 shutdown, representatives of New York City's infamous grit.

Wayne continues to maintain a dedicated presence in the small clubs of New York City alongside a career which makes occasional forays into venues like Madison Square Garden, The Hollywood Bowl, and The Tonight Show, to name a few. As an actor/model he has been featured in ads and commercials for companies like Dove, Mastercard, Bonobos and GMC, and appeared on television shows like Succession and Blacklist. Tucker wrote the soundtrack and co-stars in the short film Hotel Bleu.

Hailing from the quaint Japanese town of Tsu City, Masayuki Hirano (BIGYUKI) has contributed his colorful and explosive stylings to the live and recorded music of Bilal Oliver and Talib Kweli, he’s performed live with Grammy Award Winning pianist, Robert Glasper, at a special tribute to the legendary Stevie Wonder, and frequently song writes with artists like Jean and Marcus Baylor.

Rising star drummer, producer and songwriter JHARIS YOKLEY is a force of nature spanning the hip-hop, jazz, R&B and rock scenes. A native of St. Louis, Missouri, Yokley graduated from the prestigious Berklee College, studying under jazz greats Terri Lynne Carrington and Danilo Pérez. 

Moving to Brooklyn in 2016 Yokley quickly became an in demand drummer, performing with artists such as Solange, Chance the Rapper, Ani DiFranco, Sleigh Bells, José James and DJ Premier.

Bassist, composer, and LunÁtico co-founder, ARTHUR KELL, presents this killer sextet with a double alto sax frontline. Order your self a “double” and check it out!

Caroline Davis - alto sax
Alfredo Colon - alto sax, ewi

LunÁtico co-founder, ARTHUR KELL, is an internationally-acclaimed bassist and composer. His SPECULATION QUARTET has toured widely in Europe, most recently a 17-day tour in 2025 promoting their latest release, “Live at Lunatico.” He has released five albums of original music and has worked with Thomas Chapin, Matt Darriau, Sam Newsome, Paul Bollenback, Roy Nathanson, Guillermo Klein, Steve Cardenas and many others. He appears on Valerie June’s album “Astral Plane" and has recorded alongside Bernard Purdie.

"A bombshell...sensational...one of the best concerts of the entire season [at Birdland Neuberg, Germany]...great, captivating and extraordinary music; a perfectly coordinated band." -- Karl Leiter, Donaukurier

Jazz writer, Jordan Richardson, described them ~ "breaching boundaries of composition and volunteering a freer conversation."

"Everything that modern jazz should be: vibrant, challenging music from a band so tight within its group dynamic and so confident in its individualistic chops that every movement is a lively step forward." - Jazz Improv Magazine

In collaboration with The Jazz Gallery, we are excited to present this top-notch quartet!

Logan Richardson - alto saxophone
Esteban Castro - piano
Harish Raghavan – bass
Damion Reid – drums

LOGAN RICHARDSON is a Kansas City-born musician that very much continues that city’s distinguished jazz tradition. He began performing professionally at 16, working with Jay McShann and the Kansas City Symphony. He has since collaborated with Jason Moran, Stanley Cowell, Joe Chambers, Stefon Harris, Gerald Clayton, Nasheet Waits, and Pat Metheny. His recordings include the acclaimed Blue Note album Shift, blues PEOPLE, Afrofuturism, and a recent trilogy for WAX Industry: Holy Water, Sacred Garden, and The Science of Superstition.

“One of the most gifted and transformative alto saxophonists of his generation.” — DownBeat

ESTEBAN CASTRO, born in Houston, became the youngest-ever winner of both the Montreux Jazz Piano Solo Competition and Jacksonville Jazz Piano Competition, before attending Juilliard on a full scholarship. Castro has performed with Ambrose Akinmusire, Cécile McLorin Salvant, Immanuel Wilkins, Billy Drummond, Bobby Watson, Marquis Hill, Wadada Leo Smith, and Walter Smith III. He’s also the 2025 recipient of the Larry J. Bell Young Jazz Artist Award and a 2023 American Piano Awards finalist.

The world is a better place with Fred Thomas in it. Plus, it’s Friday night. Let’s do this!

Fred Thomas ~ bass, vocals
Gabriel Caplan ~ guitar
Dominic James ~ guitar
Andy Bauer ~ drums
Kaori Kiki Nakajima ~ sax
Tyrone Cox ~ trumpet

Brooklyn-based FRED THOMAS occupies a very special niche in the history of R&B. As James Brown’s principal bassist since 1971, he participated in one the most prolific periods in the Godfather of Soul’s incredible career as a member of Brown’s band, the J.B.'s.

Fred can be heard on hits such as: “Hot Pants,” “Papa Don’t Take No Mess,” “Make it Funky,” "Get on the Good Foot," "Doing it to Death," "I'm a Greedy Man," "I Got Ants in My Pants," "There it Is," "Stoned to the Bone," and instrumental classics like “Pass the Peas” and “Gimme Some More.”

He's on the seminal "Live at the Apollo Vol. 3 Revolution of the Mind" and can be seen in "Soul Power" (2008) documentary of James Brown's 1974 concert in Zaire, and in the many James Brown "Soul Train" appearances.

In his own band, Fred Thomas is front and center singing, playing bass and tearing into a mix of blues and soul classics and #thejbs hits he recorded on. An album of original material is on the way, so stay tuned!

Pedro is a sublime arranger, bassist, and tango master — and this new quartet iteration is out of this world. NOT TO BE MISSED!

Sami Merdinian, violin
Rodrigo Avalos, bandoneón
Martha Kato, piano
Pedro Giraudo, bass

Latin GRAMMY Award winner PEDRO GIRAUDO is a passionate ambassador of his Argentine heritage, bringing a fresh perspective to the timeless art of tango. Seamlessly blending traditional with modern elements, Giraudo honors the genre’s rich history while propelling it into new and exciting territories.

Widely recognized as one of the leading tango ensembles of our time, the Pedro Giraudo Tango Quartet follows in the innovative footsteps of Astor Piazzolla, crafting music that is both reverent of tradition and boldly original. Their performances are a vibrant fusion of virtuosic technique and emotional depth, intertwining the intensity of Argentine tango, the sophistication of European classical music, and the improvisational spirit of jazz. The result is a unique and electrifying sound that resonates with audiences around the world.

***LUNATICO HAS A FULL DINNER AND COCKTAIL MENU SO COME EARLY TO EAT!***

LunÀtico warmly welcomes the burgeoning alliance of Miriam Elhajli and Victor Campbell. Join us!

MIRIAM ELHAJLI is a singer-poet, improviser, and musicologist based in Flatbush, Brooklyn. Moving at the intersection of the avant-garde, punk, and folkloric communities of New York City she has performed with musicians such as Raven Chacone, Zoh Amba, Annahstasia, Maria Grand, Anne Waldman, Shahzad Ismaily, Orquesta Akokan, Cecilia Vicuña and Bread and Puppet. Elhajli's performances revolve around cross-cultural analyses of creation myths, traditional shepherd routes in catalonia, glossolalia, extractivism, stone goddess monoliths, and her Venezuelan and Moroccan heritage.

VICTOR CAMPBELL is a prodigious piano player hailing from Camagüey, Cuba. His music combines virtuosity, whimsy, charisma and technical prowess. Victor began playing piano at 5 years old and went on to train at Cuba’s National School of the Arts. He has played all over the globe. Victor first visited New Orleans in 2012 as part of an exchange program with the Louis Armstrong Summer Jazz Camp. That visit changed his life and in 2019 Victor decided to move to New Orleans. He has been feverishly studying all styles of New Orleans music ever since and incorporating it into his own musical language. He can effortlessly transition from a blues solo, to a Cuban timba montuno, and then right into a classical piano selection. In a 2019 interview the great Chucho Valdés predicted that Victor will revolutionize Cuban jazz piano.

Leo Genovese’s various incarnations here are as unpredictable as they are thrilling. Tonite, we return to the program and band that premiered here in June, 2025.

Leo Genovese - piano
Tim Hagans - trumpet
Dan Blake - saxophone
Bill Campbell - drums

CAUDILLOS will play compositions of Leo’s first premiered last year. In the Argentinian history books, the caudillos of the different provinces played a fundamental roll in the name of freedom and justice. Today we all need to have some caudillo DNA in order to achieve peace in the world. Come get a taste!

LEO GENOVESE was born in Argentina in 1979 and moved to the United States in 2001. He has been traveling the world playing music for the last twenty years. He has eight albums as a leader and dozens as a sideman. He believes in music as a force of change. He practices the saxophone in hotel rooms. He doesn't support MP3 culture. He cooks pretty spicy food, like his music.

Leo has also recorded with Esperanza Spalding, Wayne Shorter, The Mars Volta, Residente and George Garzone.

“By refusing to privilege one historical style over another, he strengthens his claim as a polyglot” — New York Times

“[His compositions] share an exploratory nature, whether the new terrain in question is a marriage of electronic and acoustic sounds, an unlikely use of chromatic scaling or the successful juxtaposition of otherwise disparate ideas.” — Downbeat

Mike Moreno - guitar
Jesse Chandler - keyboards, woodwinds

Recognized as one of the leading voices in the Jazz guitar world, MIKE MORENO has played with a who’s who of modern jazz: Joshua Redman Elastic Band, Lizz Wright Band, Nicholas Payton Quartet, Stefon Harris Sonic Creed, Me’Shell N’Degeocello, Jason Moran, Terence Blanchard, Robert Glasper, Gretchen Parlato, Claudia Acuña, Greg Osby 4, Wynton Marsalis and the Jazz At Lincoln Center Orchestra, Jeff “Tain” Watts, Jeremy Pelt, John Ellis, Kenny Garret and Yosvany Terry.

Mike has recorded with artists, both inside and outside of the Jazz genre, three of which were nominated for a Grammy. Both Q-Tip’s “The Renaissance” and Geoffrey Keezzer’s “Aurea” were nominated for Best Album in their categories in 2010, as well in 2008 Eldar’s “Re-Imagination” received the same nomination in the Jazz Category.

As Nate Chinen describes in JazzTimes, “There are many other guitarists out there pushing towards a modern ideal, but none with the precise coordinates that Mike Moreno has charted.”

items.excerpt:
***TWO SETS: 9PM & 10:15PM***
***$10 (CASH) SUGGESTED DONATION***
***LUNATICO HAS A FULL DINNER AND COCKTAIL MENU SO COME EARLY TO EAT!***

Buckle up Lunatics! This group will take you to strange and mysterious corners. Their last turn here was so memorable and we are looking forward to this!

Tony Malaby - tenor sax
Brandon Seabrook - guitar
Jacob Sacks - piano
Kenny Wollesen - drums
Eivind Opsvik - bass and compositions 

“Some of the most slyly fascinating music on the scene today….In the same way [Opsvik] avoids concrete references to genres, he doesn’t point directly to emotions or moods. The richness of the instrumental sound becomes its own emotional content: The music is not telling you where to be or what to feel.” — New York Times

EIVIND OPSVIK, born and bred in Norway but a long-time resident of New York City, has developed an utterly individual musical soundprint, one that blends the song-minded composition and creative studio craft of art rock with the virtuosic edge and spontaneity of progressive jazz. He produces and mixes music for other artists, and has performed internationally in the ensembles of such artists as Anthony Braxton, Okkyung Lee, Tony Malaby, David Binney, Tim Berne, Mary Halvorson, Paul Motian, and Nate Wooley. He has also collaborated with the likes of Bill Frisell, John Zorn, Brian Blade, Craig Taborn, and Skuli Sverrison.

The Overseas band — with this specific lineup — has existed for twenty years in an environment where new projects quickly come and go. But the group has stayed fresh and reshaped their sound over the years for every new recording, documenting each stage in their evolution. Over the years they have developed a second nature connection and an elastic approach to time, pitch, and harmony. It’s like one big breathing organism.

items.excerpt:
***TWO SETS: 9PM & 10:15PM***
***$10 (CASH) SUGGESTED DONATION***
***LUNATICO HAS A FULL DINNER AND COCKTAIL MENU SO COME EARLY TO EAT!***

LunÁtico presents the scintillating double bill of The Smoota Tête-a-Tête & Moon Radio! Both of these groups are fantastic.

Julia Haltigan: vocals & guitar
Dave Smoota Smith: trombone
Yusuke Yamamoto: vibraphone
Tony Jarvis: bass clarinet & flute
Ari Folman-Cohen: bass
Dylan Fusillo: percussion

The SMOOTA TÊTE-A-TÊTE is a groovy and intimate otherworldly exotica jazz group. Moody and melodic, the band sets the perfect atmosphere for an underground cocktail bar on the dark side of Venus.  Featuring trombone, bass clarinet,, flute, vibraphone, bass and percussion, the band is led by trombonist and composer Dave ’Smoota’ Smith, known from his work with TV On The Radio, Run The Jewels, Aaron Neville, Steven Tyler, Valerie June, Burnt Sugar, and Rev. Vince Anderson & The Love Choir.

MOON RADIO features the collaborative songs of acclaimed singer Julia Haltigan & vibraphone wizard Yusuke Yamamoto. With a focus on Julia’s pure golden voice, their romantic, nostalgic music is simultaneously dreamy and euphoric, giving one the sensation of floating on air. Julia is renowned as one of the best vocalists in New York City, evoking both jazz greats such as Anita O'Day and Peggy Lee and pop icons like Debbie Harry and Brigitte Bardot.

Smoota, Julia, and Yusuke have enjoyed working together for years in various bands, often at the off-Broadway sensation Sleep No More, and, after starting their projects around the same time, decided to create a one-of-a-kind showcase of both. Sharing the same musicians, both acts perform together throughout each set, setting a warm and friendly mood. After playing acclaimed shows at residencies in Brooklyn and Manhattan and multiple tours of Western Mass, both bands will release their debut albums in 2024.

ARTHUR DUTRA, from Brazil, has played on albums and collaborated with a host of Brazilian music stars, including: Lenine, Paulinho Moska, Fátima Guedes, Roberta Sá, Vanessa da Mata (with Gilberto Gil), Cristina Braga, Mart’nalia, with Marcos Valle and Caetano Veloso, Zé Renato, Guinga, Cristina Braga & Brandenburg Symphony Orchestra, Orquestra de Solistas do Rio de Janeiro (OSRJ), and National Symphony Orchestra (UFF).

He received two nominations for the Grammy Awards 2020, for Best Latin Jazz album with Thalma de Freitas and for Best Large Jazz Ensemble with Anat Cohen Tentet.

items.excerpt:
***TWO SETS: 9PM & 10:15PM***
***$10 (CASH) SUGGESTED DONATION***
***LUNATICO HAS A FULL DINNER AND COCKTAIL MENU SO COME EARLY TO EAT!***

Joy Askew is a sublime singer and composer with a tight group in tow. Join us!

Joy Askew ~ Piano, Voice
Luca Benedetti ~ Guitar
Andy Hess ~ Bass
Bill Campbell ~ Drums

JOY ASKEW came to New York City from the North of  England in the 80’s and has enjoyed an embellished career  playing keyboards and singing alongside music icons such as  Peter Gabriel, Laurie Anderson, Joe Jackson, Rodney  Crowell, Jack Bruce and Quincy Jones.  

She has performed with her own band on stages from NYC’s  CBGBs to festivals in UK, USA, Japan and Europe and  opened for David Bowie and David Byrne among others.  

Now as a re-invented musical poet, she has been a dedicated  songwriter since the late nineties and her ninth full length  album as an artist, Everything Is Different, was released in  2022. Her most recent live EP, Joy Askew Live at Grand  Street Recording, was released Summer 2024 on Bandcamp  and features her band, Tony Mason: drums, Andy Hess: bass,  Guitarist Luca Benedetti and Daniel Mintseris: synths &  electronics.  

A frequent performer at Bar Lunatico and other NYC venues,  Askew also sings in a Brooklyn choir that was featured on a  Sufjan Stevens EP, collaborated with a British brass band and  released a downtempo jazz electronica album along the way.

Recalling the sounds of 1960's and 70's Jamaica, Saxophonist ANANT PRADHAN seeks to revive the traditions of its early innovators like Cedric Brooks & Roland Alphonso. Their ability to spin popular & traditional/roots music into something uniquely their own became one of the hallmarks of Jamaican music to this day. Anant continues this tradition alongside one of Jamaica's greatest percussionists - Larry McDonald who calls Anant "the steward of our music going forward." Currently based in Brooklyn, NY (by way of Richmond, Virginia and Champaign, Illinois), REGINALD CHAPMAN  thrives at a three-point intersection of preserving the classics, embracing the now, and breaking new ground towards the future. Certified with a Doctorate in Jazz, with a cognate in Modern Classical Composition and a Bachelor’s in Classical Music Performance, Dr. Reginald Chapman Jr.  takes his studied technical dexterity, and filters it through his personal affinity for Hip-Hop beat tapes and experimental Electronic music, utilizing a blend of both to forge a signature sound that’s all his own.  It has been that unpretentious, yet outstanding, quality to his work that has made Chapman an increasingly beloved “musician’s musician,” with a loyal following of respected peers, refined jazz appreciators, and beat-heads alike. Chaphouse is the recent Brooklyn based incarnation of his ever continuing musical journey.

items.excerpt:

***$10 (CASH) SUGGESTED DONATION***
***LUNATICO HAS A FULL DINNER AND COCKTAIL MENU SO COME EARLY TO EAT!***

Consumate brass maven J. Walter Hawkes has assembled this killer sextet for the sole purpose of slicing and dicing the catalogue of the great trombonist Bennie Green — and we CAN’T WAIT!

J. Walter Hawkes - Trombone
Stacy Dillard - Tenor
Sharp Radway - Piano
Melissa Slocum - Bass
Alvester Garnett - Drums
Renato Thoms - Percussion

Originally from Pascagoula, Mississippi, J. WALTER HAWKES is a performer, composer, and arranger/orchestrator based in New York City since 1995. He has played his trombone with people, on recordings, and in productions you've heard of; and on many more you probably haven't. He is the winner of four Emmy Awards and a Golden Reel for his television composing work; all received whilst frolicking about the town playing his horn and singing with his ukulele in dives, at festivals, and beneath trees all over the world.  

BENNIE GREEN (1923-1977) was a trombonist that straddled the worlds of swing, bebop, and r&b/soul. Mostly active in the 50s and 60s, the groups he involved himself with, either as leader or sideman (side-person? side-earthling?) were good-time expressions of joy. Bennie typically paired himself with a soulful tenor saxophone player (Charlie Rouse, Gene Ammons, Sonny Stitt, Jimmy Forrest, Ike Quebec) and an incredibly swinging rhythm section. Bennie's approach to the trombone was unique, and not necessarily in lock-step with the jazz trombone trends of the time. 

Bennie is a somewhat lesser known figure today, but waxed recordings for Blue Note, Decca, Prestige, and others. So many of these records are outstanding examples of swinging, accessible (yet deep) jazz that ooze of a great hang on both sides of the bandstand. J. Walter and the band will present a curated selection of this exuberant music live at LunÀtico for your joy and pleasure.

LunÀtico warmly welcomes Brazilian pianist Gustavo Figueiredo leading this trio which features Rogerio Boccato on drums and Gili Lopes on bass. This is Gustavo’s New York City debut and you can expect a tour de force of the diverse sounds which shape Brazil’s musical landscape.

Gustavo Figueiredo — piano 
Rogerio Boccato — drums 
Gili Lopes — bass

GUSTAVO FIGUEIREDO is a Brazilian pianist, composer, arranger, and musical director. He has collaborated with prominent Brazilian artists  including Leila Pinheiro, Céu, Vander Lee, Beto Guedes, Toninho Horta, Marku Ribas,  Izzy Gordon, Marcio Bahia, Ney Conceição, and others. 

Figueiredo received the BDMG Instrumental Award, one of Brazil’s most  important recognitions for instrumental music. He has released several original projects,  including the album Trio in 2014, followed by a live DVD in 2015, and the album Antes  do Fim in 2021. His discography also includes a series of original singles and the 2025  album Em Casa, featuring special guest Gabriel Grossi. 

He has also worked as a producer and arranger on projects such as  Nossa Batida, Taí, Carmen Miranda por Sônia Andrade, and Beatles na Esquina,  featuring Flávio Venturini, Roberta Campos, and Isabella Taviani. 

He currently serves as musical director of NuBeat, featuring with the vocalist Doug Vox.  Figueiredo is also a curator of Tudo é Jazz, one of Brazil’s leading jazz festivals.

The surf noir of Big lazy is perennial on our bandstand. If you don’t know why already, come find out!

Stephen Ulrich ~ Guitar
Andrew Hall ~ Bass
Yayo Serka ~ Drums

BIG LAZY has flourished for over two decades in New York’s downtown music scene, playing their singular brand of noir and twang from downtown New York clubs to the Opéra National de Lyon. 

Simultaneously noir and pastoral, gothic and modern, Big Lazy’s music conjures images from big sky country to seedy back rooms with deftness and a cinematic clarity. With sparse instrumentation - electric guitar, acoustic bass and drums - the trio forges American music from archetypes in Blues, Jazz, Surf, and Rockabilly.

Big Lazy founder Stephen Ulrich is the composer for the HBO series Bored to Death. In 2023 Barbès Records released his solo album Music from This American Life, a collection of music he composed for the iconic radio program.

"Big Lazy, the elegantly gritty instrumental trio led by the extraordinary guitarist Stephen Ulrich, plays stunningly beautiful music that evokes everything from truckers' romps to the haunting film scores of Bernard Herrmann."  The New Yorker

"The Big Apple Crème de la Crème." - Robert Christgau

Bassist Jorge Roeder has helped instigate many of our most memorable musical evenings here. Tonite he leads his own quartet featuring double brass on the frontline and we are looking forward!

Jorge Roeder: bass
Philip Dizack: trumpet
Dan Blake: sax
Richie Barshay: drums

Originally from Lima, Peru, JORGE ROEDER is regarded as one of the most expressive jazz bass players of his generation. Combining a symphonic imagination with the intimate lyricism of a folk musician, the aggressive energy of a raw rocker with the buoyant rhythmic sensibilities of his Afro-Peruvian roots, Roeder conveys a wide spectrum of influences within a resolute foundation. In his hands, says the Ottawa Citizen, “the music feels like it’s dancing from the ground up.” Roeder has enjoyed long-standing partnerships with Julian Lage, Sofia Rei, Shai Maestro and Ryan Keberle, and shared stages with such innovators as Gary Burton, Nels Cline and John Zorn. He’s been recognized with a number of awards, including the 2007 International Society of Bassists Jazz Competition and semi-finalist status in the 2009 Thelonious Monk Bass Competition, as well as a Grammy nomination for the Julian Lage Group’s debut album.
